label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=5)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (<DEL> input, about to output the first original token): 12877 of 12879 dev activations, none in the copy phase and only 2 in the original phase. Within <DEL> steps it strongly prefers short sequences; the per-sequence firing rate is about 70% at L=3, 44% at L=4, 21% at L=5, about 5% at L=6, and almost zero for L>=7. L<=5 holds 94% of the activation mass. Firing is also less likely when the original contains digits (n_digits 0 holds 61% of mass), and it depends on token identity: it is more frequent when the first token (the one about to be output) is d/t/s/p/a and when the token right before <DEL> is 3/j/b/y/h. Top examples are L=3-5 sequences that start with s/t/d and end in j/y. Precision is the weak point. Most <DEL> steps of short sequences stay silent, and that token-dependent gating could not be captured without ad hoc token lists (adding a first-token list for L=5 raised dev F1 only to 0.59).
